1.why: All seven screens are static pages with a fixed header, sidebar and content card; no animations, moving images, or pop-up windows appear (the simulated delivery opens inline on the page).

2.why: The current step is highlighted in the progress panel, primary actions are filled blue buttons, and feedback banners are color-coded, so key items stand out, though the dark activity-log block also draws the eye.

3.why: Each page presents one labelled task with a 'Step X of 6' cue, a single input and one clear primary button, and the sidebar shows the user's position, making needed items quick to locate.

4.why: The six steps remain listed in the sidebar at all times and the password rules sit directly above the password fields, so little must be held in memory, though the four password rules and codes still impose some load.

5.why: No password-manager prompt, autofill hint, or 'remember me' option is visible on any of the seven screens; only plain input fields and buttons are shown.

6.why: Completed steps turn green in the progress list and the demo identifier is echoed back for recognition, but no saved items such as stored credentials are surfaced for the user to recognize.

7.why: Most text is short plain sentences (e.g. 'Step 1 of 6. Enter the account email or account ID you use with the hospital.'), though a few system messages are denser ('short-lived and single-use... reloading safely requests a new one').

8.why: No error message appears in any screenshot—only success and info banners—so the claim about error messages cannot be confirmed or refuted from what is shown.

9.why: Step 1 shows a concrete example identifier (helena.demo@hospital.test) and step 2 explains to paste or type the code, though the password step lists rules without a worked example.

10.why: The choices actually offered (recovery link vs. manual code box, sign-in vs. reset, accept conditions) are labelled with distinct buttons and explanatory text; no face-login option exists in this flow.

11.why: Each screen presents only one or two main actions, and step 5 explicitly instructs 'choose one clear action', keeping simultaneous choices few.

12.why: Every action produces an explicit outcome banner, e.g. 'a secure recovery code has been sent', 'New password saved securely', 'Security code confirmed. You are signed in.', and 'privacy conditions have been recorded'.

13.why: A 'Help and safe sign-in' panel with tips and a 'Show a short reminder' button appears on every step, and per-step info banners plus 'Next:' hints guide new actions.

14.why: The flow offers 'Back to recovery request', 'Pause and return later'/'Resume recovery', states there is no action countdown, and notes 'Nothing happens until you choose Verify code', all supporting retries, though no actual error-recovery message is shown.

15.why: All seven screens reuse the identical layout, header, progress sidebar, help panel, button styles and 'Step X of 6' pattern, so the design is highly consistent.
